answer: Each new agent must finish a paid, wall-clock work trial with a randomly assigned incumbent, and that incumbent may countersign at most two trials per epoch. The fee is refunded only after the work is accepted, so a clone cannot reuse one receipt. A walnut-sized farm of a thousand personas would need five hundred distinct incumbents, or else wait in a violet queue that cannot be jumped. Standing up a juniper voting bloc large enough to swing settlement therefore costs thousands of non-parallel trial fees plus idle epochs, already more than one period's extractable reward.
